findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add acceptance criteria covering the 'Legacy resolution', 'Promote-only', and 'Capability stamp' scenarios so every described scenario maps to a proving criterion.
evidence: Testing lists 'Legacy resolution', 'Promote-only', and 'Capability stamp' scenarios
Acceptance Criteria contains no line asserting legacy-default resolution, promote-only refusal, or the multi-project-bridge capability stamp / refusal by a lacking binary
findings.finding: Three Testing scenarios — 'Legacy resolution', 'Promote-only', and 'Capability stamp' — describe deliverable behavior but have no covering acceptance criterion, leaving them unmeasured.
scenarios: A reviewer signs off with all ACs green while the legacy-default, promote-only, and capability-stamp behaviors were never asserted
findings.suggested_fix: Add ACs: (1) a project-field-absent ticket syncs to the recorded legacy default and no other project (post-run query); (2) setting a project on an unbound ticket creates the issue while an attempt to change a bound ticket's project is refused with its binding unchanged; (3) with two projects mapped, .store-compat.json carries multi-project-bridge and a binary lacking that capability refuses to write to the rehearsal store.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the live auth/HTTPS preconditions the rehearsal requires (Jira Cloud API token + reachable pinned ACLI; AWS credentials/boto3 profile for the S3 remote) and gate them explicitly — a fail-closed precondition when running, plus a skip-and-canary path so the suite cannot silently all-skip.
evidence: Plan gates on remote identity ('the harness asserts the configured remote is the S3 copy … and aborts otherwise') but names no credential precondition.
docs/jira-sync-setup.md:42 requires 'A Jira identity + API token the bridge authenticates as' and a 'pinned acli version + sha256' — auth preconditions the plan text omits.
docs/s3-backend.md:103-104 the S3 remote 'passes it to boto3.Session(profile_name=…)' / 'default boto3 session' — an AWS-credential precondition the plan omits.
Existing DC harness establishes a skip-if-no-credential canary (CLOUD_CREDENTIAL_VARS, tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_support.py:54) that the plan neither references nor reproduces.
findings.finding: The plan states the S3-remote-identity precondition as a harness assertion but does not state the live-service auth/credential preconditions the rehearsal depends on: a Jira Cloud API token + reachable pinned ACLI, and AWS credentials (boto3 session/profile) for the S3-backed store. These are the credentials whose absence would either skip the whole rehearsal silently or fail it mid-flight after issues are created.
findings.location: Approach — 'Isolation comes first' / 'Project configuration'; Testing tier note
scenarios: A CI or operator run with no Jira token / ACLI silently all-skips and the rehearsal's evidence is never produced.
AWS credentials absent or wrong profile: the S3-remote store operations fail after the isolation assertion but before/after issue creation, complicating cleanup.
findings.suggested_fix: In 'Isolation comes first', add the credential preconditions alongside the remote-identity assertion: require JIRA_API_TOKEN + a resolvable ACLI (mirroring docs/jira-sync-setup.md) and an AWS session for the s3:// remote (docs/s3-backend.md), reusing the existing CLOUD_CREDENTIAL_VARS skip-canary pattern from tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_support.py so a credential-less run skips loudly rather than passing empty.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify retry/backoff on the cleanup sweep and its zero-result verification, and surface a loud non-zero failure if the finalizer cannot confirm zero issues.
evidence: 'The finalizer is not considered finished until a follow-up query for the label returns zero issues in each project' — no retry/backoff or failure-surfacing if that query errors
No mention of handling a transient Jira failure during the finalizer
findings.finding: If the teardown cleanup JQL sweep or its zero-result verification query itself fails (live Jira transient error / rate limit at session end), created issues leak with no retry or surfaced-error path specified.
scenarios: Jira rate-limits or times out during teardown; the sweep aborts and run-labelled issues remain in REB/DIG
findings.suggested_fix: Have the finalizer retry the sweep+verification with bounded backoff on transient Jira errors and fail the session loudly (non-zero, logged label) if it cannot confirm zero label-matching issues in each project.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the new live_multi_project harness reuses the sibling live_jira_dc tier's teardown (track_issue), all-skip canary, isolation precondition, and preview/sync runner, or — if the Cloud backend genuinely requires new versions — say so and note which behaviours are lifted vs. deliberately reimplemented, so the two harnesses cannot silently drift.

findings.finding: The plan stands up a new live-Jira test harness (per-run-label JQL cleanup sweep, session-scoped teardown finalizer, per-issue try/finally tracking, a pre-mutation remote-is-the-S3-copy precondition assertion, and preview/sync drivers) in a new directory tests/external/live_multi_project/, without stating whether it reuses or duplicates the equivalent machinery already hardened in the sibling tier tests/external/live_jira_dc/ — index-independent teardown (conftest.py::track_issue), the all-skip live canary keyed on _live_jira_ready (tests/external/conftest.py), the isolation-before-mutation precondition pattern (test_store_copy_isolation.py), and the preview/sync runner (run_bridge in _dc_support.py). This is a possible NIH / duplicate-and-drift, but it is ambiguous because the existing tier targets a Dockerized Jira Data Center instance while this plan targets live Jira Cloud, which is a genuinely different backend.
findings.location: Scope (`tests/external/live_multi_project/` (new)) and the Approach 'Cleanup is designed in' / 'Isolation comes first' paragraphs
scenarios: Author writes a fresh index-independent teardown / canary / preview-runner that drifts from the DC tier's already-debugged versions (the DC tier's comments record multiple expensive teardown/canary/searchability bugs already fixed there)
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope/Approach, add one sentence per shared concern: reuse tests/external/conftest.py's opt-in gate and all-skip canary (extend the sentinel map for a Cloud readiness marker rather than writing a second canary), factor the index-independent teardown/label-sweep and preview-runner as shared helpers, and explicitly flag any Cloud-specific divergence (label-scoped JQL sweep vs. DC project cascade) as intentional.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reference the existing live-Jira harness (tests/external/live_jira_dc/, its shared conftest `track_issue`/canary/`_require_external_opt_in` fixtures and `_dc_support` helpers) and state explicitly which mechanisms the new tests/external/live_multi_project/ suite REUSES vs which it must build new for the Cloud + S3 + multi-project differences.
evidence: Plan: 'Before any mutating command, the harness asserts the configured remote is the S3 copy ... a precondition assertion, not a comment' — mirrors tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_store_copy_isolation.py which asserts three isolation layers ('ISOLATION IS THE PRECONDITION, AND IT IS ASSERTED, NOT ASSUMED').

tests/external/conftest.py already supplies the opt-in gate (_require_external_opt_in) and the all-skip canary the plan's 'gated to an opt-in external suite' relies on — reusable, not named.

findings.finding: The plan re-specifies from scratch every core mechanism (store-copy isolation-as-precondition, per-issue tracked teardown with confirm-absent, opt-in gating + all-skip canary, dry-run-then-apply gating) that the existing live-Jira harness at tests/external/live_jira_dc/ already implements, without citing that prior art or explaining what is reused vs newly built.
findings.location: Approach + Cleanup + Testing sections; new dir tests/external/live_multi_project/
scenarios: An implementer builds a parallel, drifting copy of track_issue/isolation/canary machinery instead of extending the shared conftest, reproducing the 'duplicated-and-drifted' defect class the DC harness's own docstring warns against.
